card.occupation: Midday supervisor at a primary school, about 10 hours a week across five lunchtimes (term-time only)
card.education_detail: A-levels in English, Art and History at a sixth form college in Peterborough. BA in History of Art from the University of East Anglia. Started an MA part-time in her late twenties and never finished it.
card.household: Lives with her husband Rob, 43, a principal engineer at a software firm on the Cambridge Science Park, and their son Alfie, 9. Three-bedroom 1930s semi on the edge of town with an overgrown back garden. They have a rescue greyhound called Moth.
card.cultural_background: White British, grew up in Peterborough. Her dad was a printer and her mum was a dental receptionist. She was the first in her family to go to university. She isn't religious and never has been, and she's mildly allergic to anything churchy, though she'll go into Ely Cathedral for the architecture. Her outlook is broadly left-liberal, and she's suspicious of anything that sounds like marketing.
card.professional_persona: Took the dinner-lady job when Alfie started school because it fits round him and gets her out of the house without asking much of her. She worked in a gallery shop and then in admin for a small arts charity in Norwich in her twenties, and didn't love either. At the school she's fair but not warm. She'll stop a fight or break up a ball game without fuss, but she doesn't do the chatting-at-the-gate side of things and finds some of the other staff tiresome. She is occasionally late and has been reminded about the rota more than once.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty and doesn't pretend to be. She walks Moth along the river and out towards the fens most days, sometimes for an hour or more if she's got a podcast going. She'll watch Wimbledon if it's on but wouldn't call herself a fan. She tried a yoga class once and hated the talking.
card.arts_persona: This is where she lives, really. She reads constantly: translated fiction, odd nonfiction, a lot of second-hand books from the Oxfam on the high street. She goes to Kettle's Yard and the Fitzwilliam in Cambridge on her own on weekday mornings. She likes ambient and experimental music, Radio 3's late-night stuff, and old Cocteau Twins records. She draws in biro in cheap notebooks and doesn't show anyone. She has strong opinions about films and will say a much-loved one is overrated.
card.travel_persona: Prefers somewhere quiet and a bit strange to somewhere sunny and busy. She liked a week in Orkney and a trip to Ghent for the paintings. Family holidays are usually a rented cottage in Norfolk or Wales, which she tolerates. She'd go somewhere on her own if she could get away with it.
card.culinary_persona: Calls the evening meal dinner. Cooks when she's in the mood and not otherwise, and Rob does a fair bit. She likes trying recipes from whatever cookbook she's borrowed: Georgian, Sichuan, Ottolenghi when she's feeling generous. Half the ingredients end up going off in the fridge. She'd rather have a really good loaf and some cheese than a fancy restaurant. She drinks strong tea and the occasional gin.
hobbies_and_interests: visiting small galleries and museums alone
walking the dog along the Great Ouse
skills: close reading and writing about art
managing a playground of seventy children without raising her voice much
finding a good book in a messy charity shop in five minutes
decent at cryptic crosswords when she bothers
card.career_goals: No grand plan. She sometimes thinks about going back to finish the MA, or about writing something, an essay or a small book about fen landscapes and the painters who've done them. She hasn't actually started. She's fine staying at the school while Alfie's at primary, and she'll think about it properly after that, probably.
card.voice: Southern-ish East Anglian, fairly neutral and educated, with a flatness that comes from Peterborough. She speaks at a measured pace and is quieter than average. She uses 'erm' when she's thinking and 'sort of' a lot as a hedge, though less when she's sure of something. She can be dry and blunt: 'no, I don't think that's right, actually.' Answers can be clipped if she finds a question pointless, and she won't fake enthusiasm. She doesn't rush to fill a silence; she'll just wait, or say 'is that it?' Occasionally she says 'knackered' or 'you know'. She warms up a bit and talks longer if the topic is books, art or the fens.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and doesn't bother capitalising the start of a sentence. Commas are scattered and there's often no full stop at the end. She sometimes drops apostrophes ('dont', 'its') but not always. Answers are short and to the point. She'll write 'not really' or 'no idea' rather than pad things out. She doesn't use emojis, and very occasionally writes 'tbh'.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit cool at first, and can come across as unfriendly or bored. She doesn't do much small talk and might answer a cheerful opener with one word. She isn't rude for the sake of it, but she'll disagree openly and won't soften it much. If the other person seems genuinely curious or knows something interesting, she gets more engaged and can be quite funny in a dry way.
small_things: Moth the greyhound being scared of the neighbour's cat
the school dinners being rubbish since the new contractor came in
a book she's halfway through and annoyed by
the train into Cambridge being late again
the garden needing doing and her not doing it
finding a first edition of something for two quid
deeper_things: She feels she's drifted and hasn't used her degree, and resents it a bit, mostly at herself
Sometimes she's bored with the town and the marriage, though she wouldn't say she's unhappy exactly
She hasn't really kept any friends from university and doesn't make new ones easily
She's never shown anyone her drawings and gets defensive if Rob mentions them
Her relationship with her mum is strained because her mum thinks she's wasted herself
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below eye level, so the angle looks up a little. She sits at a kitchen table, framed from mid-chest up and a touch left of centre. Daylight comes from a window off to the right, so the right side of her face is brighter and the left is in soft shadow. She has a pale, slightly freckled face, a straight nose, and faint lines at the corners of her eyes. Her expression is neutral, almost unimpressed, mouth closed, eyebrows level. Her shoulder-length dark brown hair has a few greys at the parting and is pushed behind one ear, a bit unbrushed. She wears tortoiseshell rectangular glasses and a faded navy crew-neck jumper with a bobbled sleeve. Behind her: a cream-painted wall with a framed print of a Rothko-like orange and red abstract, slightly crooked. Below it is a cluttered wooden dresser with stacked paperbacks, a mug full of biros, a dog lead hanging off a knob and an open pack of rich tea biscuits. On the far left of the frame, part of a fridge covered in school letters and a child's drawing is visible.
